title: Counting the Camp
summary: At Sinai God commands a census of men twenty and older able to fight, counting 603,550 without the Levites. The tribes camp around the tabernacle in set order under their standards, with Judah on the east. The Levites are counted separately from a month old, are given to Aaron, and serve in place of the firstborn of Israel. The chapters assign the Kohathites, Gershonites and Merarites their duties in carrying the tabernacle.

title: Purity, Nazirites and the Priestly Blessing
summary: Rules cover putting the unclean out of the camp, restitution for wrongs, and the test of bitter water for a wife accused of unfaithfulness. The Nazirite vow is set out: abstaining from wine, leaving the hair uncut, and avoiding the dead for the period of the vow, followed by offerings when it ends. The section closes with the blessing Aaron and his sons are to speak: the LORD bless thee and keep thee, and give thee peace.

title: Offerings and the Passover at Sinai
summary: The tribal leaders each bring the same offerings for the altar over twelve days, and Moses hears the LORD speak from above the mercy seat. The Levites are cleansed and set apart. Israel keeps the Passover in the wilderness, and men unclean from touching a body are allowed a second Passover a month later. The cloud covers the tabernacle by day and appears as fire by night, and Israel breaks camp only when it lifts.

title: Leaving Sinai and the Complaints
summary: On the twentieth day of the second month the cloud lifts and Israel leaves Sinai in marching order, with Moses asking Hobab to guide them. The people complain, fire burns at the edge of the camp, and they weep for the meat and fish of Egypt. Moses protests that the burden is too heavy; God has seventy elders share his spirit, and Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp. Quail come in great numbers, and a plague strikes those who craved meat.

title: Miriam and Aaron Speak Against Moses
summary: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses because of the Cushite woman he married and ask whether the LORD has spoken only through him. The LORD summons the three, says he speaks to Moses face to face rather than in visions and dreams, and departs in anger. Miriam is struck with leprosy, Aaron pleads, and Moses prays for her. She is shut out of the camp for seven days, and the people wait until she is brought back.

title: The Twelve Spies
summary: Moses sends twelve men, one from each tribe, including Sethur of Asher, Joshua and Caleb, to scout Canaan, and they return with a cluster of grapes from Eshcol. Ten report giants and fortified cities; Caleb and Joshua urge Israel to go up. The people weep and talk of returning to Egypt. God threatens to disown them, relents at Moses' plea, but decrees that this generation will die in the wilderness over forty years. A presumptuous attack fails.

title: Korah's Rebellion
summary: Korah, Dathan and Abiram and 250 leaders challenge Moses and Aaron, saying all the congregation is holy. Moses tests them with incense; the ground opens and swallows Dathan, Abiram and their households, and fire consumes the 250. When the people blame Moses the next day, a plague kills 14,700 until Aaron stands with incense between the living and the dead. Aaron's rod then buds and bears almonds among twelve rods, confirming Levi's priesthood.

title: Water from the Rock at Meribah
summary: After Miriam dies at Kadesh, the people again have no water and quarrel with Moses and Aaron. Told to speak to the rock before the congregation, Moses says, 'Must we fetch you water?' and strikes it twice, and water comes out. The LORD says Moses and Aaron did not believe him enough to sanctify him before Israel, and so will not bring the congregation into the land. The water is called Meribah.

title: Edom Refuses Passage and Aaron Dies
summary: Moses sends messengers to the king of Edom asking to pass along the king's highway, promising not to touch field or well. Edom refuses and comes out with a large army, so Israel turns away. At Mount Hor the LORD tells Moses to take Aaron and his son Eleazar up the mountain; Moses strips Aaron of his priestly garments and puts them on Eleazar, and Aaron dies there. All Israel mourns him thirty days.

title: The Bronze Serpent
summary: Discouraged on the way around Edom, the people speak against God and Moses and say they loathe the light bread. The LORD sends fiery serpents, and many die. The people confess their sin and ask Moses to pray, and at God's instruction Moses makes a bronze serpent and sets it on a pole. Anyone who has been bitten and looks at it lives.

title: Victories over Sihon and Og
summary: Israel moves on through the wilderness, camping at Oboth and the valley of Zared and crossing the Arnon, the border of Moab. At Beer the LORD gives water and the people sing 'Spring up, O well'. Moses sends to King Sihon of the Amorites for passage, is refused, and Israel defeats him and takes his cities. They then defeat Og king of Bashan at Edrei and take his land, which gives Israel the territory east of the Jordan.

title: Balaam and Balak
summary: Balak, king of Moab, fears Israel and sends for the diviner Balaam to curse them. God tells Balaam not to curse, then allows him to go; on the way the angel of the LORD blocks the path, which Balaam's donkey sees before he does, and the donkey speaks. From the heights Balaam blesses Israel three times against Balak's wishes, then foretells a star out of Jacob and a scepter out of Israel, with oracles against Moab, Edom, Amalek and others.

title: Baal of Peor
summary: Israel settles at Shittim and the men begin to have relations with Moabite women and to join in the worship of Baal of Peor. The LORD commands that the leaders be hanged, and a plague breaks out. When an Israelite man brings a Midianite woman into the camp in sight of the congregation, Phinehas, Aaron's grandson, follows them into the tent and kills them with a spear. The plague stops after 24,000 have died, and Phinehas receives a covenant of peace.

title: A New Census and Joshua Appointed
summary: After the plague a second census counts 601,730 men of fighting age, and the land is to be divided by lot among them; of the earlier generation only Caleb and Joshua remain. The five daughters of Zelophehad ask for their father's inheritance since he left no sons, and the LORD rules that daughters may inherit. At Abarim God lets Moses see the land, and Moses commissions Joshua before Eleazar and the congregation by laying hands on him.

title: Vengeance on Midian
summary: At the LORD's command Israel sends 12,000 men, a thousand from each tribe, with Phinehas, to war against Midian. They kill every male, including five Midianite kings and Balaam, and take women, children and cattle. Moses is angry that the women were spared, since they led Israel astray at Peor, and orders that the boys and women who had known a man be killed. The plunder is divided between the soldiers and the congregation, and the officers bring an offering of gold.

title: Tribes Settle East of the Jordan
summary: The tribes of Reuben and Gad, rich in cattle, ask to settle in the grazing land of Jazer and Gilead east of the Jordan instead of crossing. Moses is angry and compares them to the spies who discouraged the people, but agrees on condition that their fighting men cross and fight with the other tribes until the land is conquered. They build sheepfolds and cities, and half the tribe of Manasseh also receives land east of the Jordan.

title: Borders, Levitical Cities and Cities of Refuge
summary: God tells Israel to drive out the inhabitants of Canaan and destroy their idols, and sets the boundaries of the land on all four sides, with a leader from each tribe to divide it. The Levites receive forty-eight cities with pasture land, six of which are cities of refuge, three on each side of the Jordan, for someone who kills unintentionally. The killer stays there until the high priest dies. Murder requires more than one witness, and no ransom may be taken.
